answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a per-funder rate limit enforced by memory-hard puzzles. Each new identity submits a proof seeded from a recent basalt block hash, with difficulty growing in the number of identities already funded by the same address in that window, so a thousand registrations from one wallet cost quadratically more than one. An honest user pays a walnut-sized fee once; a farm pays a rising toll per head, and the protocol's pulse of new joins stays cheap only while it stays diverse. Because the seed rotates every block, precomputed proofs go stale and cannot be amortised.
